_comment: Allowlist for backend/scripts/tenant-check.js. Every entry needs a reason. 'match' is a case-insensitive substring of the whitespace-normalised SQL (empty = every flagged statement in that file). Keep entries as narrow as possible; remove entries when the code they cover is removed (the checker reports stale entries).

entries.match: SELECT is_active FROM users WHERE id = ?
entries.reason: Session user's own row (id from the session), used to block disabled accounts; users is a global identity table.
Session user's own row after /api/switch-company verified a user_companies membership for that company.
Invite flow: look up an existing global account by e-mail after the caller was verified as admin of the company; membership is stored in user_companies with company_id.
Invitation accept: the 256-bit random token identifies the invitation; the company comes from the invitation row itself.

entries.match: UPDATE invitations SET status = ? WHERE id = ?
entries.reason: Invitation accept: the id comes from the invitation row that was just selected by its secret token.

entries.match: SELECT id, email, global_role FROM users WHERE email
entries.reason: Invitation accept: identify the invited e-mail's existing global account; company membership is created with company_id from the invitation.
Invitation accept: creates the global account; company membership is created in user_companies with company_id from the invitation.

entries.match: UPDATE invitations SET status = ? WHERE id = ?
entries.reason: Invitation id comes from a pending invitation selected for the authenticated user's verified e-mail (OAuth / provisioning).

entries.match: UPDATE users SET password = ?, invite_token = NULL
entries.reason: Set-password by secret invite token, row id comes from the token lookup above.

entries.match: SELECT id FROM users WHERE email = ?
entries.reason: Forgot-password: global account lookup by e-mail; a reset mail goes only to that address.

entries.match: UPDATE users SET password_hash = ? WHERE id = ?
entries.reason: Reset-password by secret one-time token (password_resets row), id comes from that row.
The session user's own acceptance rows (user id from the session); acceptance is per account, not per company (company_id is only the context at the time of acceptance).
Personal data export: the session user's own row (id from the session).
Anonymise: the target was loaded a statement earlier through a user_companies join filtered by company_id (FOR UPDATE), is not the actor, not a superadmin and a member of no other company.

entries.match: FROM audit_logs WHERE user_id = ? AND metadata IS NOT NULL
entries.reason: Anonymise: audit rows of the verified target user (see above); only e-mail/IP/name keys are removed from the metadata.

entries.match: UPDATE audit_logs SET metadata = ? WHERE id = ? AND user_id = ?
entries.reason: Anonymise: row id comes from the select above (rows of the verified target user).

entries.match: SELECT email FROM users WHERE id = ?
entries.reason: The authenticated user's own e-mail (id from the session) for the Stripe checkout.
Login: users is a global identity table, the company is derived afterwards from user_companies.
Signup: global username uniqueness check.
Signup: global e-mail uniqueness check.
Signup: the freshly created user's own row, inside the signup transaction.
Router is not mounted in index.js. The company_id condition is added through the conditions array (first condition), not inside the SQL literal.
The base SELECT is followed by 'AND ${table}.company_id = ?' appended with string concatenation right after (see 'query += ...company_id').

Legacy route /project-tasks/:id/comments; the task was verified to belong to the caller's company (projects join) right before. Column set does not match the current schema (task_id/company_id), so the route fails today.
Reads back the row inserted a statement earlier in the same request (insertId).
The session user's own row (/me/language).

entries.match: SELECT COUNT(*) AS count FROM user_companies WHERE user_id = ?
entries.reason: Counts the session user's own memberships (company creation limit).

entries.match: UPDATE users SET is_active = 0 WHERE id = ?
entries.reason: Target was verified as a member of the caller's company AND as manageable (not superadmin, no other company) by isManageableMember() right before.

entries.match: UPDATE users SET password_hash = ? WHERE id = ?
entries.reason: Target was verified as a member of the caller's company AND as manageable (not superadmin, no other company) by isManageableMember() right before.

entries.match: UPDATE users SET password = ?, password_hash = ? WHERE id = ?
entries.reason: /me/password: the session user's own row (current password verified, company checked).
Company id from the URL is only used after the caller's own user_companies row for that company was checked (role = admin) in the same handler.

Superadmin is cross-tenant by design: only called from routes/superadmin.js (requireSuperadmin) and re-checked there (global_role superadmin + own password). Company-scoped statements carry company_id; the remaining ones address users/company_subscriptions by id after the row was loaded by company_id (membership join / FOR UPDATE select).

Superadmin monitoring (revenue, health, audit viewer, growth): read-only cross-tenant aggregates by design; only called from routes/superadmin.js behind requireSuperadmin. Optional company_id/user_id filters of the audit viewer are validated integers passed as parameters.
Superadmin-only router (requireSuperadmin on every route); cross-tenant aggregates are intended. Reviewed separately in the superadmin work.
Platform-wide daily totals for the Slack report (cron, no tenant request context); no tenant data is exposed, only counts.
Outbox worker claims and updates rows of all companies by design (background job, ids come from its own claim query); rows are inserted with company_id.
OAuth identity lookup in global identity tables (users, user_identities) by provider subject / e-mail, before any company context exists.
Builds the session for a just-authenticated user (their own users row); company context is derived from user_companies.
Company id from the URL is only used after the caller's own user_companies row for that company is checked (admin) in the same handler.
/api/switch-company: a user_companies membership for that company is required before the session is switched.
